A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Paracosm research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: V1 reports original Paracosm experiments on CIRR, CIRCO, Fashion IQ, and GeneCIS, including component ablations and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: V3 retains original retrieval experiments on three benchmarks and reports additional efficiency, generator-comparison, and feature-weighting results.

M1.justification: The proposed pipeline and Eq. (1) remain unchanged: generate mental images and descriptions, combine query features, combine real and synthetic database features, and retrieve by cosine similarity. LongCat substitution and beta weighting are experimental analyses; the final method retains Qwen generation and equal database-feature weighting.

E1.justification: V3 removes GeneCIS entirely, including its Focus Attribute, Change Attribute, Focus Object, and Change Object tasks with small per-query galleries. CIRR, CIRCO, and Fashion IQ remain. This removes a distinct family of conditional-similarity tasks rather than merely reducing samples.

E2.justification: V3 adds evaluated AutoCIR and CoTMR comparisons in Tables 1, 3, 4, and 9. It removes OSrCIR from several corresponding backbone-specific benchmark comparisons, drops LDRE from the CLIP ViT-L/14 Fashion IQ comparison, and removes LinCIR from the OpenCLIP ViT-G/14 Fashion IQ comparison despite retaining LinCIR elsewhere.

E3.justification: Retained benchmarks keep their splits, sample counts, and retrieval metrics. New experiments introduce offline/online efficiency measurements under a stated common OpenCLIP ViT-L/14 and A100 setting, validation-set weighting sweeps, and a LongCat comparison without prompt or hyperparameter retuning. OpenCLIP ViT-G/14 evaluation already existed in v1's appendix.

E4.justification: V3 adds computational-efficiency analysis, Qwen-versus-LongCat generator testing, real/synthetic feature-weight sensitivity, and a CIRR validation curve for lambda. It removes the extensive OSrCIR backbone/LMM reproduction investigation and revises qualitative examples. The full component ablation in Table 10 is retained; the extra rows in main-text Table 5 were already present in v1's appendix.

E5.justification: Neither version reports random seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. Added experiments retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: V3 adds efficiency and new-comparator results, plus LongCat CIRR R@1 of 32.12 versus Qwen's retained 32.27. Paracosm's CLIP ViT-L/14 Fashion IQ average R@10/R@50 changes from 28.76/49.32 to 29.45/49.93. GeneCIS and numerous comparator results disappear. The prominent OpenCLIP ViT-G/14 Paracosm scores already appeared in v1 and are unchanged.

T1.justification: The task definition, feature-combination equations, and cosine-similarity retrieval rule are unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs; the new beta sweep is an empirical sensitivity analysis.

C1.justification: The central claims of training-free retrieval through mental images and synthetic database counterparts remain. V3 removes explicit claims of validation on four benchmarks, consistent with dropping GeneCIS, and qualifies the introduction's contribution statement to comparisons against zero-shot CIR approaches. The broad state-of-the-art claim remains.

C2.justification: V3 adds interpretations concerning generator independence, balanced database-feature weighting, and the tradeoff between substantial offline processing and online inference cost. Its prompt limitation shifts from ambiguous GeneCIS instructions to dataset formatting differences illustrated by CIRCO. Existing generative-fidelity limitations, societal concerns, and failure-case explanations remain.

D1.justification: V3 specifies preprocessing on 16 A100 GPUs and individual-method execution on one A100, replacing v1's A100/4090 description. It adds runtime, memory/storage information, and explicitly documents CIRR-validation tuning of lambda. The 512-by-512 generation resolution, default generation parameters, and notebook/README availability statements already existed.

R1.justification: V3 adds positioning and citations for AutoCIR, CoTMR, LongCat, and synthetic-domain adaptation work, while removing GeneCIS and the GitHub-issue references supporting the earlier backbone discussion. The central distinction from description-based and pseudo-target-image CIR methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 makes localized language and terminology revisions, expands Section 3.2 with prompt explanations previously supplied in the appendix, adds an efficiency subsection, and reorganizes the supplementary outline. An author affiliation also changes. The main narrative and six-section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The paper changes from two-column to single-column layout, redraws the overview and pipeline diagrams, redesigns and relocates prompt illustrations, restructures benchmark tables, and rearranges qualitative panels. It also adds the efficiency table and beta plot. New Figure 5 contains a mismatched staircase description between bear images.

improvement.justification: V3 improves practical documentation through measured costs, validation-based parameter reporting, and generator/weighting checks. However, it removes GeneCIS and an unexplained strong comparator: v1 Table 12 reports LinCIR Fashion IQ R@10 of 45.11 versus Paracosm's 38.74, while v3 Table 4 retains 38.74 but omits LinCIR and claims state-of-the-art performance. These gains coexist with reduced comparative completeness and a mismatched new illustration; the PDFs do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
